question: Why is key.transpose(-2, -1) preferred over key.transpose(1, 2) when implementing attention key transposition in PyTorch?
options: It automatically performs scaling by the square root of d_k during transposition.
It operates on the last two dimensions, ensuring compatibility with both 3D and 4D multi-head tensors.
It replaces masked future positions with negative infinity without requiring masked_fill.
It transposes the batch dimension with the feature dimension to speed up GPU memory access.
explanation: Using negative indexing transpose(-2, -1) dynamically selects the last two dimensions (sequence length and d_k), making the code work seamlessly for 3D tensors (batch, seq, d_k) and 4D multi-head tensors (batch, heads, seq, d_k). Hardcoding transpose(1, 2) fails on 4D tensors because index 1 is the head dimension, not sequence length.

question: In a batched attention operation, given a Query tensor of shape (1, 3, 4), Key tensor of shape (1, 3, 4), and Value tensor of shape (1, 3, 4), what are the shapes of the attention weights p_attn and the final output tensor respectively?
options: p_attn has shape (1, 4, 4) and final output has shape (1, 3, 3).
p_attn has shape (1, 3, 4) and final output has shape (1, 3, 4).
p_attn has shape (1, 3, 3) and final output has shape (1, 3, 4).
p_attn has shape (1, 3, 3) and final output has shape (1, 4, 4).
explanation: torch.matmul(query, key.transpose(-2, -1)) multiplies (1, 3, 4) by (1, 4, 3) yielding p_attn of shape (1, 3, 3). Then torch.matmul(p_attn, value) multiplies (1, 3, 3) by (1, 3, 4) producing a final output tensor of shape (1, 3, 4). Option 1 incorrectly assumes p_attn retains the input embedding shape.

question: What happens if scores.softmax(dim=-2) is used instead of scores.softmax(dim=-1) when computing attention weights?
options: Future positions will retain positive values instead of becoming 0.0 after masking.
Attention probabilities are normalized across queries per key token instead of across key tokens per query token.
PyTorch raises a runtime shape mismatch error because dim=-2 is an invalid axis index.
The softmax values will all become negative one billion (-1e9).
explanation: dim=-1 normalizes along the last axis (keys for each query), creating valid probability distributions across key tokens for each input query. Using dim=-2 normalizes along the query axis across queries for each key token, breaking the proper attention distribution per token.
